raceRatingSource: Cook Political Report / Sabato's Crystal Ball / Inside Elections (all three, as of Feb 10 2026)
primaryNote: The March 3 primary has early voting underway as of this manifest date (Feb 26). Results will not be available until March 3 election night. A runoff is triggered if no candidate clears 30% of the vote.

candidates.background: Former Governor of North Carolina (2017-2025); former NC Attorney General (2001-2017). Two-term governor, six-time statewide winner. Announced Senate bid July 28, 2025 after Tillis retirement. Overwhelming favorite in Democratic primary. Cooper leads in head-to-head polling against Whatley (Emerson, Jan 2026: +6).
candidates.notes: Dominant Democratic primary favorite; former rival Wiley Nickel suspended his campaign and endorsed Cooper after Cooper entered the race (July 2025). No credible challenger emerged. Expected to be the Democratic nominee barring extraordinary circumstances.

candidates.background: Former Chair of the Republican National Committee (2024-2025); former Chair of the North Carolina Republican Party (2019-2024). Has no prior elected office; comes from party infrastructure and political organizing. Raised $6.27 million as of Feb 11, 2026; $2.5M+ cash on hand.
candidates.notes: Endorsed by President Donald Trump before officially entering the race; appeared with Trump at rallies in Rocky Mount and Fort Bragg. Holds ~38% support in Feb 2026 GOP primary polling with ~50% undecided. Endorsed by Lara Trump (former RNC co-chair). NRSC-backed. Clear front-runner for the Republican nomination.

candidates.background: Retired U.S. Navy JAG (Judge Advocate General) officer; defense attorney who represented defendants charged in connection with the January 6, 2021 Capitol riot. From Waxhaw, NC. Raised $187,237 as of Feb 11, 2026; ~$24,000 cash on hand.
candidates.notes: Endorsed by former Lt. Governor Mark Robinson, Sidney Powell, and Michael Flynn. Second in GOP primary polling at ~7.5% (Feb 2026 Carolina Journal poll). Trails Cooper 48%-38% in hypothetical general election matchup.

candidates.background: 2024 Republican nominee for North Carolina Superintendent of Public Instruction (lost general election). Conservative activist. Raised only $10,720 as of Feb 11, 2026; ~$5,248 cash on hand.
candidates.notes: Originally entered race as grassroots alternative to Tillis; remained as challenge to Whatley. Platform includes school choice, FEMA overhaul, mail-in voting restrictions. Polling at ~1.6% in Feb 2026 GOP primary.

candidates.background: IT security engineer and Durham entrepreneur.
candidates.notes: Polling at ~0.4% in Feb 2026 Republican primary. Separately listed as Libertarian candidate for the general election by some sources — this may reflect a dual filing or a party change; confirm before general election cycle. Low public profile.

candidates.background: Businessman, Garner entrepreneur, and business consultant.
candidates.notes: Polling at ~1% in Feb 2026 Republican primary. Very limited public profile beyond filing.

candidates.background: Teacher from Smithfield, NC. Ran for North Carolina State House District 28 in 2024.
candidates.notes: Polling at ~0.6% in Feb 2026 Republican primary. Very limited public profile beyond filing.

candidates.background: Family caregiver; described as a perennial candidate in NC Democratic primaries.
candidates.notes: No meaningful polling support. Long-shot Democratic primary candidate.

candidates.background: Tech consultant; 2024 Democratic nominee for North Carolina's 8th Congressional District (lost general election).
candidates.notes: Has some prior campaign infrastructure from 2024 congressional race. Long-shot against Cooper in Democratic primary.

candidates.background: Businessman; 2020 Democratic nominee for North Carolina's 3rd Congressional District (lost general election).
candidates.notes: Has some prior campaign experience. Long-shot Democratic primary candidate.

candidates.background: Previously ran in 2022 Democratic primary for U.S. Senate in North Carolina.
candidates.notes: Perennial Democratic primary candidate. No meaningful polling support.

candidates.background: Cybersecurity specialist and systems architect. U.S. Navy veteran (1991-1997). Has worked for Visa, Microsoft, and federal government agencies. Master's degree in cybersecurity from University of Delaware. Based in Apex, NC.
candidates.notes: Running as Libertarian; platform focused on privacy, government modernization, and accountable governance. Appears directly on general election ballot without a primary; Libertarian Party does not hold a primary in NC.

candidates.background: Iraq War veteran; U.S. Marine Corps (2000-2004). Firefighter. From Illinois originally; associate degree from John Wood Community College.
candidates.notes: Green Party candidate for general election. Platform is anti-war and pro-social services; pledges to accept no corporate donations. Green Party does not hold a NC primary — goes directly to general ballot.

candidates.background: Consultant and social media personality. Born and raised in Durham, NC. Bachelor of Science in Management from University of Phoenix (2024). 15+ years in telecommunications, wireless services, nonprofit management. Previous 2024 candidate in Maryland.
candidates.notes: Running as unaffiliated independent in the general election. Limited campaign infrastructure and fundraising. Goes directly to general ballot as unaffiliated candidate without a primary.

withdrew.name: Wiley Nickel
withdrew.background: Former U.S. Representative, NC-13 (2023-2025); lost 2024 re-election. Former NC State Senator. Was the first Democrat to announce a Senate campaign (April 9, 2025).
withdrew.reason: Suspended Senate campaign after Roy Cooper entered the race (July 28, 2025). Endorsed Cooper and announced candidacy for Wake County District Attorney instead.

withdrew.name: Margot Dupre
withdrew.reason: Disqualified by North Carolina State Board of Elections following a residency challenge; failed to prove NC residency. Ballot printed before disqualification — name appears on primary ballot but vote does not count.
